news.headline: Irving supplied 17 points (7-15 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), six rebounds, five assists and two steals over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 116-94 win over Golden State.
news.story: After sitting out the second game of a weekend back-to-back set, Irving returned to action and delivered decent numbers. The veteran point guard has scored in double digits in all 12 of his games this season, and he's contributed at least five boards and five assists in three of his seven November contests, averaging 22.9 points, 4.1 assists, 3.9 rebounds, 3.4 threes and 1.4 steals.

news.headline: Irving (knee) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
news.story: Irving didn't play in Sunday's 131-94 loss to Boston, the second game of a back-to-back for the Mavericks. He will return Wednesday for the meeting with Golden State, likely resulting in Naji Marshall heading back to the bench.

news.headline: Irving (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Celtics.
news.story: Irving was listed as questionable to face Boston after playing 37 minutes during Saturday's 127-117 loss in Cleveland. He will, however, sit out the second leg of the back-to-back for Dallas, which will likely send Cooper Flagg's usage to the moon. Naji Marshall and Walter Clayton should also get a boost in minutes and playmaking responsibilities off the bench.

news.headline: Martin racked up 12 points (4-8 FG, 4-5 3Pt), five rebounds, five assists and two steals in 34 minutes during Sunday's 131-94 loss to the Celtics.
news.story: Martin made all four of his field goals from three-point range and contributed across several categories despite Dallas' lopsided defeat. His 34-minute workload was particularly encouraging, and while the Mavericks' inconsistent rotation makes it difficult to determine whether that level of involvement will continue, he's logged 30-plus minutes in back-to-back games. Martin has never been a particularly prolific scorer, but performances featuring contributions in rebounds, assists and steals are more likely to make him relevant in deeper fantasy formats than occasional hot shooting nights.

news.headline: Martin supplied 15 points (6-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and one steal across 33 minutes during Saturday's 127-117 loss to the Cavaliers.
news.story: Martin started for the fifth straight game, turning in what was easily his best performance of the season. Prior to this game, Martin had scored a total of nine points in his previous five games, a fair indication that this effort should be viewed as nothing more than an outlier.

news.headline: Martin is in the starting lineup for Friday's matchup with the Jazz, Christian Clark of The Athletic reports.
news.story: Martin will replace Zaccharie Risacher in the first unit for Friday's game. In his previous start this season, Martin finished with five points, six rebounds and one three-pointer over 21 minutes.

news.headline: Flagg chipped in 33 points (11-15 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 8-8 FT), five rebounds, nine assists and four steals across 34 minutes during Wednesday's 116-94 victory over the Warriors.
news.story: This was Flagg's 10th career game with at least 30 points and five assists, and it was his fourth 30-plus performance of the season. The 19-year-old has gotten off to a hot start with averages of 24.2 points, 6.6 rebounds, 6.4 assists, 1.4 triples, 2.0 steals and 0.7 swats per contest on 48.5 percent shooting from the field and 89.5 percent at the line, which has been good enough for top-eight value in fantasy leagues.

The veteran guard made a greater impact as a facilitator, dishing out at least 10 assists for the sixth time this season. On the year, Young is averaging 17.9 points, 8.9 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 1.2 steals through 15 appearances.

news.headline: VanVleet finished Wednesday's 119-104 victory over Indiana with 15 points (6-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt), six assists, two rebounds and one steal over 27 minutes.

He has recorded at least six assists in two of his last three outings and six times this season. VanVleet is averaging 14.0 points, 4.9 assists, 2.5 rebounds, 3.1 threes and 0.8 steals over 29.2 minutes per game in November.

news.story: Gobert has grabbed seven or fewer rebounds in three of his last four games, an unusual slump for the veteran center. His 35-minute workload is encouraging, but inconsistent rebounding and shot-blocking have diminished his fantasy impact.

news.headline: Gobert finished with 18 points (5-10 FG, 8-14 FT), 15 rebounds, three assists and two blocks in 32 minutes during Monday's 106-98 victory over the Trail Blazers.
news.story: Gobert left points on the table at the charity stripe, though he still erupted for a season-high mark in points while finishing as Minnesota's second-leading scorer. The big man also led all players in rebounds, securing his third double-double of the campaign. He's grabbed double-digit boards in six of his seven outings this month, during which he's averaged 9.1 points, 11.1 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.6 blocks in 28.9 minutes per tilt.

news.story: Jakucionis has emerged as a bright spot for Milwaukee, scoring at least 20 points in consecutive appearances after reaching double figures just twice in his previous nine games. The second-year guard has averaged 22.5 points, 4.0 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 3.5 three-pointers over his last two contests while shooting 62.5 percent from the field. His improved offensive production and increased playing time make him an intriguing fantasy option in deeper leagues, although his role remains worth monitoring.

news.headline: Fears totaled 22 points (9-20 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds, five assists and one block over 38 minutes during Friday's 126-120 loss to the Thunder.
news.story: Fears tied Zion Williamson for the team lead in scoring and tied his season high in minutes. The finish was rough: Jared McCain blocked his driving layup, and his three-point attempt to cut the deficit to one fell short. With Dejounte Murray (ankle) still sidelined, the second-year guard is running the offense full-time and averaging 15.6 points and 5.4 assists.

news.headline: Fears finished with 16 points (6-12 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 31 minutes before fouling out of Wednesday's 122-109 loss to the Pistons.
news.story: Fears was unable to finish the game after fouling out, but the second-year floor general posted an impressive stat line that included two defensive contributions. Fears is locked in as the Pelicans' starting point guard more than ever after Dejounte Murray asked for a trade, and he's averaging 17.1 points, 5.2 rebounds, 6.0 assists and 1.0 steals per game since the beginning of November.

news.headline: Kuminga totaled 23 points (7-13 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 7-7 FT), three rebounds, three assists and three blocks in 35 minutes during Thursday's 102-99 loss to the Knicks.
news.story: Kuminga was held out of Tuesday's matchup against the Trail Blazers due to a shoulder injury, but he was cleared to suit up Thursday evening. He made it clear that the issue is no longer bothering him, as the 24-year-old led Minnesota in scoring while also chipping in on the defensive end. Kuminga recorded multiple swats for just the second time through 15 appearances this season.

news.headline: Kuminga (shoulder) is available for Thursday's game against New York.
news.story: Kuminga sustained a right shoulder contusion in Monday's 106-98 loss to Portland and wasn't available for the rematch Tuesday. After carrying a questionable designation throughout the day, he has now been cleared to suit up for the meeting with the defending champs. The 24-year-old has appeared in 14 regular-season games for Minnesota in 2026-27, all of them starts, averaging 12.4 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.1 steals while shooting a career-best 39.3 percent from deep over 30.5 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Kuminga (shoulder) is questionable for Thursday's game against the Knicks, Charlie Walton of ZoneCoverage.com reports.
news.story: After missing Tuesday's game against Portland, Kuminga now has a chance to return Thursday from a bruised shoulder. His status will affect Terrence Shannon's streaming appeal most prominently in fantasy leagues.

news.headline: Wagner chipped in 35 points (13-25 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 7-9 FT), five rebounds, seven assists and one block in 36 minutes during Friday's 113-111 win over the Nets.
news.story: Wagner got whatever he wanted all night long, and he iced the game with a 15-foot step-back jumper from the right wing with 2.8 seconds left in regulation. This was his fifth 30-plus point performance of the season, and his second straight game shooting over 50 percent from the field. Over the past seven games, Wagner has been pumping out top-five numbers with averages of 31.3 points, 7.3 rebounds, 8.3 assists, 1.9 triples, 1.1 steals and 0.7 blocks per contest on 51.3 percent shooting from the field and 91.7 percent at the stripe.

news.headline: Wagner closed with 27 points (12-22 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-3 FT), eight rebounds, 11 assists, two blocks and two steals in 36 minutes during Wednesday's 121-116 loss to Philadelphia.
news.story: Wagner has scored at least 20 points in six consecutive games, continuing to shoulder a significant offensive workload with Paolo Banchero (ankle) sidelined. The versatile forward has recorded at least nine assists in three of his last four appearances, including two double-doubles, while averaging 30.3 points during that four-game stretch. His expanded playmaking responsibilities and consistent scoring have elevated his fantasy ceiling, particularly in points and assists.

news.headline: Wagner finished with 27 points (12-22 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-3 FT), eight rebounds, 11 assists, two steals and two blocks over 36 minutes in Wednesday's 121-116 loss to Philadelphia.
news.story: Wagner had trouble getting his shots from deep to fall versus the 76ers. However, the 2021 No. 8 overall pick had another quality showing and nearly scored at least 30 points for the fourth time in his last five appearances. Wagner is now averaging a career-best 24.4 points in 14 regular-season games in 2026-27, though his scoring contributions could drop once Paolo Banchero (ankle) is cleared to get back on the floor.

news.headline: Embiid totaled 26 points (7-18 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 12-14 FT), six rebounds, seven assists, three blocks and two steals over 36 minutes during Wednesday's 121-116 victory over the Magic.
news.story: With Tyrese Maxey (foot), Jaylen Brown (hamstring) and Dean Wade (hamstring) sidelined, Embiid assumed greater offensive responsibility. His seven assists reflected increased playmaking duties, while five defensive stats bolstered his fantasy production. The expanded workload is encouraging, though his usage could normalize once Philadelphia's injured starters return.

news.story: Gilgeous-Alexander was spectacular again Friday, posting his fourth 40-point game and his second in the last four outings. He's poured in 30-plus points in five straight contests, giving him an average of 36.4 points to go along with 3.6 rebounds and 3.8 assists per game over that stretch. Gilgeous-Alexander will continue to dominate touches while the Thunder find their bearings.

news.headline: Gilgeous-Alexander finished with 34 points (14-29 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 5-10 FT), five rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks over 36 minutes in Wednesday's 117-112 loss to the Hawks.
news.story: Gilgeous-Alexander scored over 30 points for the fourth consecutive game, and the multi-time MVP made just below half of his shots. Oklahoma City has now dropped four of its last five games. With injuries being a major issue for the club, Gilgeous-Alexander will likely be even more involved for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign. However, that could result in fewer quality shot attempts compared to previous seasons.

news.headline: Brooks amassed 18 points (7-14 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-3 FT), three rebounds and three assists over 25 minutes before fouling out of Friday's 111-101 win over the Jazz.
news.story: Brooks followed up his big night in Sacramento on Wednesday with another productive outing. He tied Miles Bridges for second on the team in scoring. The veteran forward has been one of the league's most accurate three-point shooters this season, at nearly 45 percent. Even on a night when the long ball wasn't falling, he found other ways to contribute.

news.story: Brooks followed Monday's 15-point performance against Denver with his strongest offensive outing of the season while matching Devin Booker for the team lead in scoring. This was the first time Brooks reached the 20-point threshold since Nov. 5, when he had 24 points in a win over the Magic. news.story: Brooks struggled from inside the arc, making just three of his 11 two-point attempts, but his perimeter shooting and defensive intensity helped Phoenix secure an important road win. The veteran also spent considerable time defending Jamal Murray, who needed 19 field-goal attempts to score 28 points. Brooks can still provide useful scoring and three-point production, though his aggressive shot selection can make him a liability in leagues that reward shooting percentages.

news.headline: Young ended with 11 points (2-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-7 FT), one rebound, eight assists and one steal across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 103-99 win over the Raptors.
news.story: Young endured his third straight game with fewer than 15 points, and it's becoming increasingly clear that performances like his 37-point outburst against the Pistons on Nov. 12 will be outliers. Young remains Washington's primary playmaker, as his eight assists helped compensate for the poor shooting, but sharing offensive responsibilities with Anthony Davis and the team's developing young players means he doesn't need to carry the scoring burden every night. He's averaging 15.6 points and 8.1 assists per game since November, although he's shooting just 33.3 percent from deep in that stretch.

news.headline: Young tallied 13 points (3-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 12 assists, two rebounds and two steals over 33 minutes in Monday's 136-120 loss to Memphis.
news.story: After going scoreless in Sunday's loss, Young reached double figures but continued to struggle with his efficiency as a shooter. The veteran guard made a greater impact as a facilitator, dishing out at least 10 assists for the sixth time this season. On the year, Young is averaging 17.9 points, 8.9 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 1.2 steals through 15 appearances.

news.headline: VanVleet contributed 25 points (10-21 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 2-5 FT), one rebound, nine assists and one steal in 33 minutes during Friday's 133-124 loss to the Nuggets.
news.story: VanVleet posted a season high in scoring and nearly finished with a double-double. He also banked in a 51-foot three-pointer at the final buzzer, though it came far too late to matter. The veteran point guard has steadily found his rhythm over the past week.

news.headline: VanVleet finished Wednesday's 119-104 victory over Indiana with 15 points (6-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt), six assists, two rebounds and one steal over 27 minutes.
news.story: It was a solid bounce-back performance for VanVleet after the veteran point guard posted only eight points during Monday's loss to the Heat. He has recorded at least six assists in two of his last three outings and six times this season. VanVleet is averaging 14.0 points, 4.9 assists, 2.5 rebounds, 3.1 threes and 0.8 steals over 29.2 minutes per game in November.

news.headline: VanVleet (knee) is off the injury report for Monday's game against Miami.
news.story: Coming off 2025 ACL surgery, the veteran point guard sat out the front end of this back-to-back set but is good to go for the second part Monday. Reed Sheppard should fall into a lesser role with VanVleet back in the fold, though Amen Thompson (knee) is questionable.

news.headline: Carter amassed 15 points (5-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and one block in 32 minutes during Wednesday's 121-116 loss to Philadelphia.
news.story: Carter has scored in double figures in three consecutive games, averaging 12.3 points and 6.3 rebounds during that stretch. The veteran center has also connected on multiple three-pointers for the first time in November, providing an additional dimension to his offensive production. With Paolo Banchero (ankle) sidelined, Carter should continue seeing consistent minutes in Orlando's frontcourt, offering steady fantasy value in points and rebounds.

news.story: Carter turned in another underwhelming performance, continuing his decline after a rapid start to the season. He has been a top-70 player thus far, but in four appearances over the past week, his rank has fallen well outside the top 100. During that time, he has averaged 9.8 points, 7.3 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in 29.7 minutes per game.

news.headline: Poeltl closed Tuesday's 111-102 loss to the Knicks with three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one steal over 18 minutes.
news.story: Poeltl continues to see his role diminish, logging fewer than 19 minutes in consecutive games after averaging nearly 30 minutes over his previous three appearances. The veteran center has moved to a reserve role behind Collin Murray-Boyles, limiting his opportunities to contribute consistently. Poeltl's reduced playing time significantly lowers his fantasy ceiling despite his rebounding ability.

news.headline: Gordon logged 18 points (6-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 5-5 FT), three rebounds and two assists over 31 minutes during Friday's 133-124 victory over Houston.
news.story: Gordon was efficient as usual, and his alley-oop finish off a Nikola Jokic pass in the closing seconds put an exclamation point on the win. The veteran forward has settled into a complementary role this season, averaging 11.6 points and 4.8 rebounds over 14 games.

news.headline: Gordon contributed 13 points (5-10 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 3-6 FT), eight rebounds, two assists and one steal in 31 minutes during Wednesday's 105-101 victory over Boston.
news.story: Gordon collected four offensive rebounds after grabbing just one total board against Phoenix on Monday. His increased activity on the glass helped offset another modest scoring performance. With Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray commanding offensive touches, Gordon's fantasy value hinges on rebounding, defensive contributions and efficient finishing rather than consistent scoring volume.

news.headline: Gordon recorded 11 points (4-6 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 1-2 FT), a rebound and an assist across 24 minutes in Monday's 117-105 loss to the Suns.
news.story: Gordon was efficient with his limited opportunities, but his six field-goal attempts and single rebound made for a disappointing fantasy performance. Denver continues to lean heavily on Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray to generate offense, leaving Gordon with a more complementary scoring role. His ability to finish around the basket and connect from beyond the arc can still provide value, but performances like Monday's illustrate how limited his production can be when he isn't contributing on the glass.

news.headline: Poeltl will start Wednesday's game against the Wizards.
news.story: Poeltl came off the bench for the previous two games, but he will return to a starting role due to RJ Barrett (hamstring) and Scottie Barnes (groin) being out. Over his last four starts, Poeltl holds averages of 13.0 points, 8.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.5 blocks and 1.3 steals in 29.8 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Poeltl closed Tuesday's 111-102 loss to the Knicks with three points (1-3 FG, 1-2 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one steal over 18 minutes.
news.story: Poeltl continues to see his role diminish, logging fewer than 19 minutes in consecutive games after averaging nearly 30 minutes over his previous three appearances. The veteran center has moved to a reserve role behind Collin Murray-Boyles, limiting his opportunities to contribute consistently. Poeltl's reduced playing time significantly lowers his fantasy ceiling despite his rebounding ability.

news.headline: Poeltl isn't starting Sunday's game against the Knicks, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
news.story: Poeltl will come off the bench for the second time this season, as the Raptors are electing to roll with Collin Murray-Boyles at center. Poeltl finished with eight points, five rebounds and one assist across 19 minutes in his previous appearance as a reserve Nov. 4 against Denver.

news.headline: McCain logged 18 points (7-14 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds, one block and one steal in 30 minutes during Friday's 126-120 win over New Orleans.
news.story: McCain gave the Thunder steady scoring for a second straight night and made the defensive play of the game. He blocked a Jeremiah Fears layup in the final half-minute and grabbed the last rebound to seal it. The third-year guard has settled into a starting role while Oklahoma City deals with a long list of injuries. He's averaging 13.7 points and has been one of the team's more dependable scorers.

news.story: McCain bounced back from a 12-point outing against Sacramento, connecting on four triples while logging at least 30 minutes for the fifth consecutive game. The 22-year-old guard has scored at least 18 points in four of his last six appearances, providing solid fantasy value through scoring and three-point production despite limited assists.

news.headline: Fears totaled 22 points (9-20 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds, five assists and one block over 38 minutes during Friday's 126-120 loss to the Thunder.
news.story: Fears tied Zion Williamson for the team lead in scoring and tied his season high in minutes. The finish was rough: Jared McCain blocked his driving layup, and his three-point attempt to cut the deficit to one fell short. With Dejounte Murray (ankle) still sidelined, the second-year guard is running the offense full-time and averaging 15.6 points and 5.4 assists.

news.headline: Fears finished with 16 points (6-12 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 31 minutes before fouling out of Wednesday's 122-109 loss to the Pistons.
news.story: Fears was unable to finish the game after fouling out, but the second-year floor general posted an impressive stat line that included two defensive contributions. Fears is locked in as the Pelicans' starting point guard more than ever after Dejounte Murray asked for a trade, and he's averaging 17.1 points, 5.2 rebounds, 6.0 assists and 1.0 steals per game since the beginning of November.

news.story: With Tyrese Maxey (foot), Jaylen Brown (hamstring) and Dean Wade (hamstring) sidelined, Embiid assumed greater offensive responsibility. His seven assists reflected increased playmaking duties, while five defensive stats bolstered his fantasy production. The expanded workload is encouraging, though his usage could normalize once Philadelphia's injured starters return.

news.headline: Kuminga totaled 23 points (7-13 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 7-7 FT), three rebounds, three assists and three blocks in 35 minutes during Thursday's 102-99 loss to the Knicks.
news.story: Kuminga was held out of Tuesday's matchup against the Trail Blazers due to a shoulder injury, but he was cleared to suit up Thursday evening. He made it clear that the issue is no longer bothering him, as the 24-year-old led Minnesota in scoring while also chipping in on the defensive end. Kuminga recorded multiple swats for just the second time through 15 appearances this season.

news.headline: Kuminga (shoulder) is available for Thursday's game against New York.
news.story: Kuminga sustained a right shoulder contusion in Monday's 106-98 loss to Portland and wasn't available for the rematch Tuesday. After carrying a questionable designation throughout the day, he has now been cleared to suit up for the meeting with the defending champs. The 24-year-old has appeared in 14 regular-season games for Minnesota in 2026-27, all of them starts, averaging 12.4 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.1 steals while shooting a career-best 39.3 percent from deep over 30.5 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Kuminga (shoulder) is questionable for Thursday's game against the Knicks, Charlie Walton of ZoneCoverage.com reports.
news.story: After missing Tuesday's game against Portland, Kuminga now has a chance to return Thursday from a bruised shoulder. His status will affect Terrence Shannon's streaming appeal most prominently in fantasy leagues.

news.headline: Jakucionis logged 18 points (6-11 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-5 FT), three rebounds, two assists and one steal over 22 minutes during Thursday's 124-114 loss to the Trail Blazers.
news.story: Jakucionis has scored at least 18 points in three consecutive appearances, capitalizing on increased offensive opportunities in Milwaukee's struggling rotation. His perimeter shooting and ability to create offense have strengthened his case for additional minutes. However, his reserve role and inconsistent playing time remain obstacles to dependable fantasy production.

news.headline: Jakucionis produced 20 points (6-8 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds, five assists and two steals over 26 minutes during Wednesday's 137-130 loss to Miami.
news.story: Jakucionis has emerged as a bright spot for Milwaukee, scoring at least 20 points in consecutive appearances after reaching double figures just twice in his previous nine games. The second-year guard has averaged 22.5 points, 4.0 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 3.5 three-pointers over his last two contests while shooting 62.5 percent from the field. His improved offensive production and increased playing time make him an intriguing fantasy option in deeper leagues, although his role remains worth monitoring.

news.headline: Gilgeous-Alexander recorded 40 points (14-24 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 8-11 FT), three rebounds, seven assists and one block in 37 minutes during Friday's 126-120 win over the Pelicans.
news.story: Gilgeous-Alexander was spectacular again Friday, posting his fourth 40-point game and his second in the last four outings. He's poured in 30-plus points in five straight contests, giving him an average of 36.4 points to go along with 3.6 rebounds and 3.8 assists per game over that stretch. Gilgeous-Alexander will continue to dominate touches while the Thunder find their bearings.

news.headline: Gilgeous-Alexander finished with 34 points (14-29 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 5-10 FT), five rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks over 36 minutes in Wednesday's 117-112 loss to the Hawks.
news.story: Gilgeous-Alexander scored over 30 points for the fourth consecutive game, and the multi-time MVP made just below half of his shots. Oklahoma City has now dropped four of its last five games. With injuries being a major issue for the club, Gilgeous-Alexander will likely be even more involved for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign. However, that could result in fewer quality shot attempts compared to previous seasons.

news.headline: Young ended with 11 points (2-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 6-7 FT), one rebound, eight assists and one steal across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 103-99 win over the Raptors.
news.story: Young endured his third straight game with fewer than 15 points, and it's becoming increasingly clear that performances like his 37-point outburst against the Pistons on Nov. 12 will be outliers. Young remains Washington's primary playmaker, as his eight assists helped compensate for the poor shooting, but sharing offensive responsibilities with Anthony Davis and the team's developing young players means he doesn't need to carry the scoring burden every night. He's averaging 15.6 points and 8.1 assists per game since November, although he's shooting just 33.3 percent from deep in that stretch.

news.headline: Young tallied 13 points (3-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 12 assists, two rebounds and two steals over 33 minutes in Monday's 136-120 loss to Memphis.
news.story: After going scoreless in Sunday's loss, Young reached double figures but continued to struggle with his efficiency as a shooter. The veteran guard made a greater impact as a facilitator, dishing out at least 10 assists for the sixth time this season. On the year, Young is averaging 17.9 points, 8.9 assists, 2.9 rebounds and 1.2 steals through 15 appearances.

news.headline: Carter amassed 15 points (5-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and one block in 32 minutes during Wednesday's 121-116 loss to Philadelphia.
news.story: Carter has scored in double figures in three consecutive games, averaging 12.3 points and 6.3 rebounds during that stretch. The veteran center has also connected on multiple three-pointers for the first time in November, providing an additional dimension to his offensive production. With Paolo Banchero (ankle) sidelined, Carter should continue seeing consistent minutes in Orlando's frontcourt, offering steady fantasy value in points and rebounds.

news.headline: Carter produced 10 points (3-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds and one assist across 28 minutes during Monday's 115-105 victory over Boston.
news.story: Carter turned in another underwhelming performance, continuing his decline after a rapid start to the season. He has been a top-70 player thus far, but in four appearances over the past week, his rank has fallen well outside the top 100. During that time, he has averaged 9.8 points, 7.3 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in 29.7 minutes per game.
